semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: PDF pages 11-12, printed pages 694-695, contain Theorem 4.4, equation (4.4), the conventional Cholesky updates, and equations (4.5a)-(4.5b).
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The translation addresses the computed upper-triangular Cholesky factor, the two local residual estimates, and the exact backward relation with both componentwise bounds.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The selected paper version and passages are the correct source for the translated result.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 4.4 uses an n by n symmetric floating-point matrix A, its computed n by n factor RHat, and an n by n real perturbation DeltaA, with one-based indices.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The translation quantifies n and a run containing real n by n matrices A and R with representable entries, then existentially quantifies one real n by n DeltaA. Indices use Fin n.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Representable real entries encode membership in the floating-point set, and the zero-based Fin n indexing has the intended dimension and one-based correspondence.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper assumes symmetry, successful Cholesky execution, and absence of underflow and overflow, then derives the local estimates (4.5a)-(4.5b) before obtaining (4.4).
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The universally quantified run must already contain off-diagonal and diagonal execution witnesses whose fields include the local residual inequalities later repeated as conclusions.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Substantive consequences of the paper hypotheses have been moved into the quantified run's antecedent. This changes quantifier scope and makes the translated conditional weaker.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 4.4 assumes a symmetric floating-point A, completion of the conventional Cholesky algorithm, and no underflow or overflow; it does not assume the error estimates it proves.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: D036 and D037 require the relevant local error inequalities as constructor fields. The run also uses an abstract Safe predicate rather than the paper's stated no-underflow/no-overflow condition.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The translation strengthens the hypotheses with the central local bounds and does not faithfully state the paper's exceptional-range hypothesis.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Equation (4.4) gives the exact identity, the row-scaled componentwise bound, and the uniform bound; equations (4.5a)-(4.5b) give the local off-diagonal and diagonal estimates.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: All two local families, the exact identity, and both bounds for the same DeltaA witness appear as translated conclusions.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The mathematical conclusion components are complete. Symmetry of DeltaA follows from the translated identity and symmetry assumptions, as in the paper.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper uses transpose, ordinary matrix multiplication, entrywise absolute value and order, finite inner sums, and arbitrary binary-tree summation order.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: D006-D010 and the mathematical definitions unfold the matrix operations and componentwise magnitude product; D040-D053 unfold the rounded reduction-tree machinery.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The dependency ledger interprets all target-relevant nontrivial operators, including the distinction between ordinary matrix multiplication and componentwise absolute values.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: RHat denotes computed floating-point entries, while RHat^T RHat, A, and DeltaA in (4.4) are related in exact real arithmetic.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: Rounded operations occur inside the execution records, their outputs are identified with entries of R, and the matrix product and backward identity are exact real expressions.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Computed values, rounded operations, exact products, and the perturbation are kept distinct.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The proof specifies the conventional upper-triangular, column-by-column Cholesky quotient and square-root updates, permitting arbitrary evaluation orders for their sums.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: For every i<j and every j, D020-D021 identify R entries with outputs of executions having exactly the corresponding prior-column products, pivot division, diagonal square root, and arbitrary reduction tree.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The collection of entrywise execution witnesses gives an extensional linkage to the conventional algorithm. The separate problem that these witnesses assume error estimates is assessed under hypotheses and relation strength.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Equation (4.4) and its scalar derivation use entrywise inequalities; |RHat^T||RHat| is an ordinary matrix product and no matrix norm occurs.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The translation uses scalar absolute values for each entry and defines P_ij as the full sum of |R_ki||R_kj|.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The componentwise, non-normwise semantics are preserved.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The one-based constants are iu off the diagonal, (j+1)u on the diagonal, (i+1)u in row i of the sharp matrix bound, and (n+1)u globally.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: With zero-based indices, the translation uses (i+1)u off the diagonal, (j+2)u on the diagonal, (i+2)u in row i, and (n+1)u globally.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Each shifted coefficient and summation endpoint is exactly the zero-based form of the paper's coefficient and endpoint.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The paper uses a standard finite radix-beta, precision-p floating-point set, round-to-nearest with arbitrary tie-breaking, and explicitly excludes underflow and overflow during execution.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: D017 permits an arbitrary finite Rep predicate and arbitrary Safe predicate; the exponent bounds are disconnected from both, representability need not be symmetric, and no global no-underflow/no-overflow assertion is present.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Nearest rounding on Safe inputs and the unit-roundoff equation capture part of the model, but Safe is not defined to express the paper's range conditions and the admitted formats need not be standard floating-point systems.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The local inequalities and matrix backward bound are consequences of the paper's arithmetic and execution hypotheses.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The execution records assume the local inequalities, after which the displayed local conclusions are projections and the matrix bounds follow by symmetry, triangularity, and coefficient monotonicity.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Although equality directions and numerical inequalities match, the theorem-level logical relation is weaker because its main numerical estimates are antecedents.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Equation (4.4) is a componentwise backward-error result measured against |RHat^T||RHat|, not a forward-error or normwise estimate.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The translation introduces DeltaA through R^T R=A+DeltaA and bounds each |DeltaA_ij| against the componentwise product formed from the computed R.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The backward-error notion and its reference quantity are preserved.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: Theorem 4.4 has constants linear in u, no O(u^2) remainder or gamma denominator, no smallness restriction, and an exact backward identity.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: Every translated coefficient is linear in u, the identity is exact, and no higher-order term or smallness condition is introduced.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The higher-order treatment matches the paper.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The source theorem concerns standard finite real floating-point arithmetic and its successfully completed Cholesky executions.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: The translation ranges over abstract formats whose Rep and Safe predicates may not describe any standard floating-point set, while restricting runs through preassumed residual certificates.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: This is not a justified faithful generalization or specialization: the arithmetic domain is broadened abstractly while the substantive numerical claim is restricted by stronger hypotheses.

semantic_checklist.paper_evidence: The nontrivial content of the proof is deriving (4.5a)-(4.5b) from rounding analysis and then assembling the matrix bound.
semantic_checklist.translation_evidence: D036 and D037 store those same local bounds in every admissible execution. The first two conclusions therefore repeat assumptions, and the remaining conclusions are algebraic consequences of them.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Admissible positive-dimensional runs can exist, but the translated theorem obtains its core numerical content for an unintended circular reason. It is also vacuous whenever no structured run can be supplied.

translation_implies_paper.reasoning: The translation cannot recover the paper's result from symmetry, successful conventional execution, and absence of underflow and overflow because constructing its run already requires the local residual estimates that the paper derives. Its abstract Rep/Safe format also does not enforce the paper's numerical model.

paper_implies_translation.reasoning: For source-admissible executions, equations (4.5a)-(4.5b) supply the translated local estimates after zero-based reindexing, and symmetry plus upper triangularity yields the exact DeltaA identity and both matrix bounds. More generally, the translated conclusions are already algebraic consequences of the stronger run hypotheses.

findings.paper_evidence: The proof of Theorem 4.4 invokes Lemmas 4.1 and 4.3 to derive equations (4.5a)-(4.5b) from the floating-point execution.
findings.translation_evidence: D036 and D037 include the corresponding residual inequalities as fields required for every off-diagonal and diagonal execution witness.
findings.impact: The translation does not establish the central rounding-error result from the paper hypotheses; it reduces the proposition to repeating assumed local bounds and assembling them into a matrix bound.

findings.paper_evidence: The source assumes a standard radix-beta, precision-p floating-point set and excludes underflow and overflow, with round-to-nearest and arbitrary tie-breaking.
findings.translation_evidence: Rep and Safe are abstract predicates with weak axioms, exponent limits are disconnected from them, representability is not required to be symmetric, and Safe is not identified with absence of underflow and overflow.
findings.impact: The translated run type admits numerical systems outside the paper's model and fails to express a required source hypothesis, so its apparent generality is not the same theorem.

rationale: The translation correctly reproduces the dimensions, zero-based index shifts, conventional update formulas, exact-versus-computed distinction, componentwise product, constants, backward-error identity, and absence of higher-order terms. It is nevertheless not faithful because each execution witness assumes the local residual inequality that the paper's rounding analysis proves, while its abstract Rep/Safe format does not encode the stated standard floating-point and range model. Consequently the paper result entails the translated conditional, but the translated proposition cannot recover the paper result.
